# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->
This proposal outlines the development of open-source R package for converting or constructing Likert items from vectors or data frames, particularly from non-standard data structures. This proposal eliminates fragmented, manual workarounds for non-standard Likert-type data by introducing a reproducible workflow that mitigates data manipulation risks. The project is for a nine-month timeline and a budget of USD8,500. The timeline is divided into two-month inception phase to design the architecture, a four-month coding and testing phase to release the core engine, a two-month preliminary release phase for initial CRAN submission and documentation setup, and a final month for project closure. The budget directly funds labor at USD50 per hour, documentation hosting, and a sensitization workshop for faculty and students at the Federal University of Technology, Minna. Upon completion, the package and its continuous updates will be maintained publicly in GitHub and CRAN repositories.
